data.title: Germany's Allane 9M operating revenue rises on leasing, service segment growth
data.description:
Overview

  • Germany vehicle leasing firm's 9M 2026 operating revenue rose 18.8% yr/yr to EUR 501.2 mln

  • Pretax profit for 9M 2026 increased 10.6% to EUR 19.4 mln

  • Company confirms full-year 2026 revenue and earnings guidance

Outlook

  • Allane confirms 2026 operating revenue guidance of EUR 670 mln to EUR 720 mln

  • Company maintains 2026 EBT forecast at EUR 25 mln to EUR 35 mln

  • Allane expects only slight contract portfolio growth in 2026 after loss of major fleet customer

Result Drivers

  • CAPTIVE LEASING GROWTH - Co said expansion in Captive Leasing segment drove contract portfolio up 42.2% yr/yr

  • HIGHER LEASING AND SERVICE REVENUE - Co attributed operating revenue growth to increased leasing revenue and usage-based service revenue in Leasing business

  • VEHICLE SALES REVENUE - Revenue from sale of returned leased vehicles and fleet management marketing rose 28.3% yr/yr

data.title: European Insurers Might Face Difficult Year Ahead — Market Talk
data.description: European insurers are likely to face challenges in 2027, with relative valuations at all-time highs, J.P. Morgan analysts write. The sector outperformed in 2026 despite JPM's cautious view, the analysts note, with a strong rerating in valuations in the second half of the year. As a result, valuations are now high, but earnings revisions are lagging, and there is a poor property & casualty pricing environment in the commercial sector and reinsurance, the analysts note. JPM says it is difficult to be positive about insurers heading into 2027, and maintains its cautious stance. JPM prefers life insurance stocks, which might benefit from structural growth drivers. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)

data.title: China markets surge as Beijing unleashes 'national team'
data.description:
Chinese stocks leapt to their largest gains in more than two years on Friday and the yuan rallied after Beijing vowed to strengthen the role of the state-backed "national team" in helping to stabilise a market that has struggled this year.

The "national team" is markets' nickname for China's state-backed investors, usually led by Central Huijin, the domestic unit of sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp, which are often buyers at times of market stress.

The Shanghai Composite index , lately languishing around 17-month lows, shot up to close about 3.7% higher, while tech and AI indexes leapt even further.

The STAR semiconductor index (.CSI950125) jumped by a near-record 19.5%. Hong Kong's technology index surged 6%. Here is what market participants said:

BENJAMIN HO, STRATEGIST, MIB SECURITIES HK, HONG KONG:

"This morning, the national team was already starting to accelerate its exercise, and the market went all out during afternoon trading.

"What we need to see is policy and supportive measures that trickle down to the broader economy."

WINNIE WU, HEAD OF ASIA EQUITY STRATEGY AND CO-HEAD OF CHINA EQUITY RESEARCH, BANK OF AMERICA GLOBAL RESEARCH, HONG KONG:

"With very depressed valuations and the consensus bearishness on China tech, it actually doesn't take too much for a relief rally. The State Council is essentially giving that confidence to say that we care about the market, we'll stabilise the market, and bring in long-term capital.

"We think giving this message from the very top level, i.e. the State Council, is an attempt to re-instill some confidence, stabilise liquidity and stabilise the trajectory of the market.

"So we think there's probably this awareness that AI is strategically, economically and financially very important, and they don't want to see a big fallout in this space."

KENNY NG, STRATEGIST AT CHINA EVERBRIGHT SECURITIES INTERNATIONAL, HONG KONG:

"It's a shot in the arm for markets. Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south.

"It's obvious that A-shares have reached a level that's gotten the regulators' attention too — that sends the market a pretty clear signal.

"But there's a lot of news affecting the market ... and so I don't think the development from here depends entirely on this one factor."

KENNETH GOH, DIRECTOR OF PRIVATE WEALTH MANAGEMENT, UOB KAY HIAN, SINGAPORE:

"The move was to boost market confidence. The market is in a technical bear market and the national team wants to ensure the market stabilises and to prevent negative spillovers.

"It's positive in the short term but the sustainability of it will depend on other factors like consumer demand and confidence, as well as investors’ views of future prospects. Exports seem okay for now. But challenges remain, such as trade barriers and restrictions on trade."

WEI LI, HEAD OF MULTI-ASSET INVESTMENTS, BNP PARIBAS SECURITIES (CHINA), SHANGHAI:

"The recent massive surge in trading volume across Hong Kong and China markets signals a significant shift in sentiment. While debate persists regarding whether we have hit the bottom, the data suggests a highly constructive evolution in market dynamics.

"While the National Team provides the foundation, today's activity shows a healthy rotation toward growth ... we are seeing a transition from leveraged speculation to high-quality participation from institutional and industrial capital.

"This combination of reliable state support and growing organic demand creates a robust environment for long-term market recovery."

CHARU CHANANA, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST, SAXO, SINGAPORE:

"There is an increasingly clear signal that Chinese authorities are uncomfortable with the extent of the equity market selloff. State-backed buying alongside other policy measures signal a growing determination to stabilise markets.

"However, I would distinguish between a turning point in policy resolve and a turning point in market fundamentals. There is a difference between authorities putting a floor under the market and creating the conditions for a sustained bull market.

"A policy-induced bounce needs to evolve into a fundamentally driven recovery before we can confidently call it a durable bottom."

JASON CHAN, STRATEGIST, BANK OF EAST ASIA, HONG KONG:

"It's very rare that Executive meeting of the State Council would make such direct comments. Last time it happened was 2024 when they rolled out a liquidity support package.

"Authorities' determination to halt the slide is definitely there. But if you're asking whether this money alone is enough to really lift the whole market, I don't think it's that simple.

"To help markets stage a medium- to long-term upward trend, more practical support policies, whether for the economy or for certain industries, are needed ... I think they really need to follow up on these, instead of just paying lip service."

data.title: Turkey's central bank suspends repo auctions in liquidity-tightening move
data.description:
Key points:
  • Net international reserves fell sharply last week
  • Central bank has hiked foreign exchange-for-lira swap auctions
  • Turkey's main banking index down 5.2% on Friday

By Nevzat Devranoglu

Turkey's central bank has suspended its one-week repo auctions temporarily in a move expected to push overnight interest rates towards the 39% overnight lending rate, tightening liquidity after heavy forex sales and a sharp fall in reserves.

In another step aimed at supporting lira demand, the central bank also said overnight it had raised the remuneration rate it pays on required reserves for deposits to 90% of the weighted average funding cost from 86%.

The moves come as authorities seek to contain the fallout from an investment funds crisis, which has prompted demand for foreign currency and a flight by some investors towards safer assets.

The lira was slightly weaker on Friday, trading at 50.7875 against the dollar and at record lows. It has weakened around 2% over the past month.

Turkey's main banking index (.XBANK) was down 5.2% on Friday.

The repo move effectively shifts funding costs above the central bank's 36% policy rate. The overnight reference rate TLREF had risen to 37.87% on Thursday from 35.95% previously.

Data on Thursday showed the central bank's net international reserves fell by $17.1 billion last week to $24.19 billion, the second-largest weekly decline on record, with reserves falling to their lowest level since May 2024.

The central bank sharply increased its daily foreign exchange-for-lira swap auctions from the usual $500 million to $2 billion on Monday, $3 billion on Tuesday, $4 billion on Wednesday and $6 billion on Thursday.

Ankara is meanwhile moving to strengthen financial oversight, appointing a new head of the banking watchdog BDDK after the resignation of Sahap Kavcioglu in connection with the funds crisis. At a press conference on the funds crisis on Thursday evening, Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said further steps would be taken to strengthen market supervision and oversight.

Three traders told Reuters earlier this week that the central bank's forex sales had exceeded $10 billion, while net reserves excluding swaps had turned negative.

Simsek said on Thursday the central bank and government would not hesitate to use various instruments to preserve the attractiveness of the lira, while Central Bank Governor Fatih Karahan said earlier this week the bank would take a proactive, flexible and controlled approach to reserve and liquidity management.

data.title: French economy contracts more than expected in third quarter
data.description:
France's economy contracted by 0.2% in the third quarter, final data from statistics office INSEE showed on Friday, more than the preliminary estimate for a 0.1% decline.

The contraction in the euro zone's second-largest economy was also below the average forecast of -0.1% in a Reuters poll of 22 economists.

  • Exports fell 1.6%, after rising 2.9% in the previous quarter

  • Household consumption rose 0.3%, compared with a 0.2% increase in the second quarter

  • A decline in investment sped up to 0.9% after falling 0.5% in the previous three months

  • INSEE said annual carry-over growth stood at 0.1% at the end of the third quarter

  • The Bank of France said earlier in November that the economy should avoid a recession and return to "moderate" growth in the fourth quarter

data.title: AI Equity Selloff Likely Had Limited Impact on Asian Economies — Market Talk
data.description: The recent artificial intelligence-related equity selloff has yet to make a dent in Asia's exports, ANZ Research analysts say in a report. South Korea's first 20-day export data for November shows demand continues to be strong, driven by semiconductors. Vietnam's export data for the first half of November also depict robust demand. "Hence, this suggests that the AI selloff is currently a financial-market shock and not a real-economy shock," ANZ says. The region is supported by existing orders and production schedules in the near-term, they add. However, ANZ notes that scheduled orders for 2027 or 2028, depend on whether companies remain willing and able to finance enormous investment needed to build the AI infrastructure.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Indian firms utilising only 20%-30% of free trade agreement benefits, RBI governor says
data.description:
Indian businesses are using only about 20%-30% of the benefits available under free-trade agreements (FTAs) compared with their foreign counterparts, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said at an event in Mumbai on Friday.

The comments come days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi said ⁠Indian industry should take advantage of opportunities from the free-trade agreements India has signed, including those with the EU and the UK

"The government of India has now opened up a number of avenues. A number of FTAs have been signed. At the same time, however, it has been found that only about 20% to 30% of the utilization has been done by Indians vis-à-vis 60% to 70% by our partners in the trade agreements," Malhotra said at an event for small and medium businesses

There is a long way to go for Indian businesses to take advantage of the lower tariffs negotiated under the agreements, he said

Small and medium businesses should learn more about the FTAs to improve quality, delivery timelines, standards and certifications, Malhotra added

The micro, small and medium enterprises sector has an AI adoption rate of about 14%, behind peers such as China, Malhotra said

India has free-trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand. Its proposed free-trade agreement with the European Union is expected to accelerate market-access opportunities and investment ⁠flows between India and the ⁠27-member EU bloc

Separately, India's Trade Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that India and the US were close to wrapping up a long-anticipated trade deal

PM Modi told industry leaders last week that Indian businesses could not take their huge domestic market for granted and urged them to compete globally in an era when resources were being weaponised.

data.title: Eurozone Bond Yields Track Treasury Yields, Oil Prices Higher — Market Talk
data.description: Eurozone government bond yields rise on what is shaping up to be a busy day for issuance and data. Upward pressure on yields comes from rising U.S. Treasury yields and higher oil prices. Italy will hold an up to 8 billion euro auction of 2032- and 2036-dated nominal bonds, or BTPs, and 2034- and 2035-dated floating-rate notes, or CCTeu. The day has already delivered flash estimate French and Spanish inflation data for November, among other data. The 10-year German Bund yield rises 2.4 basis points to 3.281%, while yields on peer eurozone 10-year bonds rise less than that, according to Tradeweb. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: Taiwan raises 2026 GDP growth projection to 13.28% on strong AI demand
data.description:
Key points:
  • 2026 GDP estimate +13.28 vs previous +11.05%
  • 2026 CPI estimate +2.07% vs previous +2.07%
  • 2027 GDP forecast +6.51% vs previous +6.04%

Taiwan's economy is expected to expand by 13.28% in 2026, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Friday, raising its outlook from a previous estimate of 11.05%, boosted by strong AI demand.

Taiwan plays a leading role in fulfilling the demand for AI chips and technology from firms like Nvidia and Apple , with the island being home to the world's largest contract chip manufacturer, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co .

Demand for AI already drove Taiwan's economy in 2025 to expand 8.76%.

The agency also revised up its third-quarter 2026 economic growth view to 14.39% from a preliminary reading of 14.36%.

For next year, it said it expected Taiwan's economy to grow 6.51%, upgrading its August prediction of 6.04%.
